extracted.intended_audience: Regulated entities and their legal/compliance staff — drug manufacturers and quality control labs, mortgagees/lenders and HUD staff, taxpayers and corporate tax counsel managing QBUs, and petitioners/wineries seeking viticultural-area designation
extracted.subtask_description: Excerpts of final rules and regulatory provisions published in the Federal Register covering (inter alia) drug assay test methods, HUD mortgage-assignment and forbearance requirements for Hawaiian Home Lands, IRS regulations defining a Qualified Business Unit (QBU), and ATF criteria for establishing a viticultural area.

rubrics_metrics.name: Erythromycin content assay (test and sample-preparation procedure)
rubrics_metrics.description: Proceed as directed in § 436.105 of this chapter, preparing the sample for assay as follows: Remove an accurately measured representative volume of the suspension and dilute with sufficient methyl alcohol to give a concentration of 2.5 milligrams per milliliter (estimated). Dilute the entire mixture with sufficient 0.1M potassium phosphate buffer, pH 8.0 (solution 3), to give a concentration of 1.0 milligram of erythromycin base per milliliter (estimated). Hydrolyze in a 60 °C constant temperature water bath for 2 hours or at room temperature for 16 to 18 hours. Further dilute with solution 3 to the reference concentration of 1.0 microgram of erythromycin base per milliliter (estimated).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow §436.105 assay procedures; the chunk provides explicit stepwise sample-preparation dilutions, hydrolysis conditions (temperature/time alternatives), and reference concentration for final assay (1.0 µg/mL).

rubrics_metrics.name: Sulfisoxazole content assay
rubrics_metrics.description: Proceed as directed in § 436.328 of this chapter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The rule cross-references the sulfisoxazole assay method at §436.328; practitioners must follow that section's procedures for sulfisoxazole content determination.

rubrics_metrics.name: pH testing of drug as prepared for dispensing
rubrics_metrics.description: Proceed as directed in § 436.202 of this chapter, using the drug as it is prepared for dispensing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: pH measurement must follow the specified method in §436.202 and be performed on the final preparation as prepared for dispensing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acceptance of assignment — general (§203.350(a) linking to §203.650)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Secretary will accept an assignment of any mortgage covering a one- to four-family residence if the Secretary finds that the criteria for acceptance of an assignment under § 203.650 have been satisfied.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: §203.350(a) was revised to reflect the statutory requirement that the mortgagor have reasonable prospects for repayment (as anticipated in TMAP). Acceptance is governed by the detailed criteria set out in §203.650 (refer to that section for substantive eligibility rules).

rubrics_metrics.name: Assignment of mortgages insured pursuant to section 247 (Hawaiian Home Lands) (§203.350(c))
rubrics_metrics.description: Notwithstanding paragraph (a), the Secretary will, upon application by the mortgagee, agree to accept an assignment of any mortgage insured pursuant to section 247 of the National Housing Act where the mortgagor has been in default for more than 180 days, provided that the requirements of §203.665 are satisfied.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This provision creates a special assignment pathway for Hawaiian Home Lands mortgages: default >180 days plus satisfaction of §203.665 requirements (which includes submission of documents showing §203.604 requirements are met). It implements the TMAP-published text independent of TMAP's effective status.

rubrics_metrics.name: Filing assignment for record (timing requirement) (§203.350(e))
rubrics_metrics.description: Within 30 days of the Secretary’s written agreement to accept assignment of a defaulted mortgage, or within such additional time as the Secretary authorizes in writing, the mortgagee must file the assignment for record.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is a mandatory procedural requirement tied to assignment acceptance; information-collection approvals related to this paragraph are noted elsewhere and OMB control numbers will be or have been published.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pre-application documentary showing that §203.604 requirements are met (mortgages on Hawaiian Home Lands) (§203.665(a))
rubrics_metrics.description: Before a mortgagee requests the Secretary to accept assignment (under §203.350(c)) of the mortgage insured pursuant to section 247, the mortgagee must submit documents showing that the requirements of §203.604 have been met.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mortgagees seeking assignment for Hawaiian Home Lands must provide documentary proof that prerequisite requirements (as set out in §203.604) have been satisfied before HUD will consider the assignment request.

rubrics_metrics.name: Forbearance eligibility and information submission (§203.654(b))
rubrics_metrics.description: The Secretary will make forbearance relief available to a mortgagor where the mortgage is assigned in accordance with §203.350(c), if all of the conditions of §203.650(a)(3) through (a)(6) are met, and none of the conditions specified in §203.650(b)(1) or (b)(2) exist, and the mortgagor and mortgagee furnish the Secretary, within 15 days of the date of the Secretary’s request, all the information requested to assist in a preliminary determination of whether or not to forbear.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Eligibility for forbearance depends on satisfying specified subsections of §203.650 (both affirmative and negative criteria) and timely provision of requested information (15-day deadline). The amount forborne, duration of reduced/suspended payments, reviews, and post-forbearance payment terms will follow policies for assignments accepted under §203.650.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interest-rate limitation on assignment-assistance repayment (relation to VA rate / §230(a))
rubrics_metrics.description: Any interest rate charged by the Secretary on repayment of assistance provided under the assignment program may not exceed the interest rate chargeable under section 230(a) for the TMAP program (the rate established for VA-guaranteed mortgages). For amounts forborne, the rate shall be the lower of the interest rate of the insured mortgage or the rate established under section 1803(c) of title 38 (VA rate), to be determined at the time the assignment is accepted by the Secretary.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This implements the 1987 statutory amendment tying the cap on assignment-assistance interest to the VA rate; HUD revised §203.654(b) to state the limitation and that the applicable rate is fixed at assignment acceptance to avoid exceeding the statutory cap if market rates later decline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Paperwork-Reduction Act / information-collection approvals (timing and nonenforcement until OMB approval)
rubrics_metrics.description: Information collection requirements contained in specified sections (e.g., §§203.350(c), 203.665(a) and (b), and §203.350(e)) have been approved by OMB under control numbers noted; the collection contained in §203.350(e) has been submitted to OMB for expedited review and, until approval, no person may be subjected to a penalty for failure to comply.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The rule lists OMB control numbers, provides an annual public reporting-burden estimate (respondents, frequency, average response time, estimated annual burden), and instructs where to send comments on burden estimates (HUD Rules Docket Clerk and OMB Desk Officer).

rubrics_metrics.name: Qualified Business Unit (QBU) — general definition (§1.989(a)-1(b)(1))
rubrics_metrics.description: A QBU is any separate and clearly identified unit of a trade or business of a taxpayer provided that separate books and records are maintained.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is the fundamental definitional test for QBU status; further application rules specify which persons and activities qualify and the required records.

rubrics_metrics.name: QBU — persons and activities that qualify (§1.989(a)-1(b)(2))
rubrics_metrics.description: A corporation is a QBU; an individual is not a QBU. A partnership, trust, or estate is a QBU of a partner or beneficiary. Activities of an entity qualify as a QBU if (A) the activities constitute a trade or business; and (B) a separate set of books and records is maintained with respect to the activities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The regulation expands QBU to include partnerships, trusts, estates and branches; the status may be treated differently depending on the taxpayer (e.g., a trust is a QBU of beneficiaries).

rubrics_metrics.name: QBU — trade or business determination (§1.989(a)-1(c))
rubrics_metrics.description: A trade or business for purposes of section 989(a) is generally any specific unified group of activities that constitute (or could constitute) an independent economic enterprise carried on for profit, the expenses related to which are deductible under section 162 or 212. Activities merely ancillary to a trade or business will not constitute a trade or business, and activities of an individual as an employee by themselves are not considered to constitute a trade or business.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Determination depends on all facts and circumstances; a vertical/functional/geographic division of the same trade can be a trade or business for QBU purposes if it otherwise qualifies. A trade or business ordinarily includes collection of income and payment of expenses and all operations that are part of the enterprise.

rubrics_metrics.name: QBU — separate books and records requirement (§1.989(a)-1(d))
rubrics_metrics.description: Except as provided in paragraph (d)(2), a separate set of books and records shall include books of original entry and ledger accounts, both general and subsidiary, or similar records. Examples describe cash-receipts-and-disbursements journals for cash-method taxpayers and sales and expenses journals for accrual-method taxpayers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Illustrative detail is provided about what constitutes books of original entry and ledgers; for purposes of the special rule on effectively connected income, books and records used to determine effectively connected income or loss satisfy this requirement.

rubrics_metrics.name: QBU — special rule for activities producing effectively connected income (§1.989(a)-1(b)(3))
rubrics_metrics.description: Any activity (wherever conducted and regardless of its frequency) that produces income or loss that is, or is treated as, effectively connected with the conduct of a trade or business within the United States shall be treated as a separate QBU, provided the books and records requirement is satisfied.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This treats certain foreign activities (or discrete activities) that generate effectively connected income as separate QBUs even if they would otherwise not be separate businesses; paragraph (d)(2) clarifies the records required in such cases.

rubrics_metrics.name: QBU — illustrative examples to guide application
rubrics_metrics.description: The regulation provides multiple examples (corporate branches, foreign subsidiaries and branches, employee courier activities, investment activities of individuals, foreign corporations treated as domestic, disposition of U.S. real property interests) demonstrating how the QBU definition, trade-or-business test, and books-and-records requirement are applied.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples show borderline cases: ancillary employee activities do not constitute QBU, but a wholly-owned subsidiary or branch that maintains separate records and carries on trade operations does; investment activities generating deductible section 212 expenses may qualify as QBU; disposition activities treated as effectively connected income may be separate QBU.

rubrics_metrics.name: Criteria for establishing an American viticultural area (AVA)
rubrics_metrics.description: An American viticultural area is a delimited grape growing region distinguishable by geographical features, the boundaries of which are delineated in subpart C of part 9. Any interested person may petition ATF to establish a grape-growing region as a viticultural area.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Establishment allows use of the viticultural-area name as an appellation of origin on wine labels and advertising to help consumers identify and growers/winemakers distinguish their products. Petitioners must follow procedures in part 9 (subpart C) and demonstrate distinguishable geographical features and mapped boundaries.

rubrics_metrics.name: Regulatory findings and certifications (NEPA, Executive Orders, Regulatory Flexibility)
rubrics_metrics.description: The rule contains findings such as a Finding of No Significant Impact under NEPA (24 CFR part 50), determinations under Executive Order 12291 that the rule is not a 'major rule,' certification under the Regulatory Flexibility Act that the rule does not have a significant economic impact on a substantial number of small entities, and other Executive Order determinations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These findings are procedural/legal certifications accompanying the rule to explain applicable analyses (or reasons analyses are not required) and where supporting documents (e.g., Finding of No Significant Impact) can be inspected.
